items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to simple linear regression with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

# Production statistical hypothesis test: Simple Linear Regression
def conduct_ab_significance_test(control_conversions, control_visitors,
                                  variant_conversions, variant_visitors,
                                  alpha=0.05) -> dict:
    # 1. Sample Conversion Proportions
    p_ctrl = control_conversions / control_visitors
    p_var = variant_conversions / variant_visitors
    
    # 2. Pooled Probability
    pooled_p = (control_conversions + variant_conversions) / (control_visitors + variant_visitors)
    pooled_se = np.sqrt(pooled_p * (1 - pooled_p) * (1/control_visitors + 1/variant_visitors))
    
    # 3. Z-Statistic and Two-Sided P-Value
    z_stat = (p_var - p_ctrl) / pooled_se
    p_val = 2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(z_stat)))
    
    return {
        "control_rate": round(p_ctrl, 4),
        "variant_rate": round(p_var, 4),
        "relative_lift_pct": round(((p_var - p_ctrl) / p_ctrl) * 100, 2),
        "z_score": round(z_stat, 3),
        "p_value": round(p_val, 5),
        "statistically_significant": p_val < alpha
    }

# Test output:
# print(conduct_ab_significance_test(120, 1000, 160, 1000))

# Production statistical hypothesis test: Statistical Assumptions and Diagnostics
def conduct_ab_significance_test(control_conversions, control_visitors,
                                  variant_conversions, variant_visitors,
                                  alpha=0.05) -> dict:
    # 1. Sample Conversion Proportions
    p_ctrl = control_conversions / control_visitors
    p_var = variant_conversions / variant_visitors
    
    # 2. Pooled Probability
    pooled_p = (control_conversions + variant_conversions) / (control_visitors + variant_visitors)
    pooled_se = np.sqrt(pooled_p * (1 - pooled_p) * (1/control_visitors + 1/variant_visitors))
    
    # 3. Z-Statistic and Two-Sided P-Value
    z_stat = (p_var - p_ctrl) / pooled_se
    p_val = 2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(z_stat)))
    
    return {
        "control_rate": round(p_ctrl, 4),
        "variant_rate": round(p_var, 4),
        "relative_lift_pct": round(((p_var - p_ctrl) / p_ctrl) * 100, 2),
        "z_score": round(z_stat, 3),
        "p_value": round(p_val, 5),
        "statistically_significant": p_val < alpha
    }

codeSnippet.code:
// Production DAX Measure: Measures of Central Tendency
Revenue YoY Growth % = 
VAR CurrentPeriodRevenue = 
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_Sales[NetRevenue]),
        Dim_Date[IsCurrentFiscalYear] = TRUE()
    )
VAR PriorPeriodRevenue = 
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_Sales[NetRevenue]),
        SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR(Dim_Date[FullDate])
    )
RETURN
    DIVIDE(
        CurrentPeriodRevenue - PriorPeriodRevenue,
        PriorPeriodRevenue,
        0
    )

items.title: Frequency Distributions
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to frequency distributions with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

# Production statistical hypothesis test: Frequency Distributions
def conduct_ab_significance_test(control_conversions, control_visitors,
                                  variant_conversions, variant_visitors,
                                  alpha=0.05) -> dict:
    # 1. Sample Conversion Proportions
    p_ctrl = control_conversions / control_visitors
    p_var = variant_conversions / variant_visitors
    
    # 2. Pooled Probability
    pooled_p = (control_conversions + variant_conversions) / (control_visitors + variant_visitors)
    pooled_se = np.sqrt(pooled_p * (1 - pooled_p) * (1/control_visitors + 1/variant_visitors))
    
    # 3. Z-Statistic and Two-Sided P-Value
    z_stat = (p_var - p_ctrl) / pooled_se
    p_val = 2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(z_stat)))
    
    return {
        "control_rate": round(p_ctrl, 4),
        "variant_rate": round(p_var, 4),
        "relative_lift_pct": round(((p_var - p_ctrl) / p_ctrl) * 100, 2),
        "z_score": round(z_stat, 3),
        "p_value": round(p_val, 5),
        "statistically_significant": p_val < alpha
    }

# Test output:
# print(conduct_ab_significance_test(120, 1000, 160, 1000))

items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to interpreting statistical summaries with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

# Production statistical hypothesis test: Interpreting Statistical Summaries
def conduct_ab_significance_test(control_conversions, control_visitors,
                                  variant_conversions, variant_visitors,
                                  alpha=0.05) -> dict:
    # 1. Sample Conversion Proportions
    p_ctrl = control_conversions / control_visitors
    p_var = variant_conversions / variant_visitors
    
    # 2. Pooled Probability
    pooled_p = (control_conversions + variant_conversions) / (control_visitors + variant_visitors)
    pooled_se = np.sqrt(pooled_p * (1 - pooled_p) * (1/control_visitors + 1/variant_visitors))
    
    # 3. Z-Statistic and Two-Sided P-Value
    z_stat = (p_var - p_ctrl) / pooled_se
    p_val = 2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(z_stat)))
    
    return {
        "control_rate": round(p_ctrl, 4),
        "variant_rate": round(p_var, 4),
        "relative_lift_pct": round(((p_var - p_ctrl) / p_ctrl) * 100, 2),
        "z_score": round(z_stat, 3),
        "p_value": round(p_val, 5),
        "statistically_significant": p_val < alpha
    }

codeSnippet.code:
-- Production analytical metric specification: Events and Sample Spaces
SELECT 
    DATE_TRUNC('month', transaction_date) AS reporting_month,
    product_category,
    COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS active_purchasers,
    SUM(quantity) AS units_sold,
    ROUND(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 2) AS total_gross_revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(net_profit_usd), 2) AS total_net_profit,
    ROUND(SUM(net_profit_usd) / NULLIF(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 0) * 100, 2) AS profit_margin_pct
FROM enterprise_analytics.fact_transactions
WHERE transaction_date >= '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1 DESC, total_net_profit DESC;

sections.title: 4. Formulas, Syntax & Hands-On Production Implementation
sections.explanation: The verified production syntax below demonstrates how to compute and evaluate conditional probability using enterprise analytics tools with strict precision and defensive error handling:

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

# Production statistical hypothesis test: Conditional Probability
def conduct_ab_significance_test(control_conversions, control_visitors,
                                  variant_conversions, variant_visitors,
                                  alpha=0.05) -> dict:
    # 1. Sample Conversion Proportions
    p_ctrl = control_conversions / control_visitors
    p_var = variant_conversions / variant_visitors
    
    # 2. Pooled Probability
    pooled_p = (control_conversions + variant_conversions) / (control_visitors + variant_visitors)
    pooled_se = np.sqrt(pooled_p * (1 - pooled_p) * (1/control_visitors + 1/variant_visitors))
    
    # 3. Z-Statistic and Two-Sided P-Value
    z_stat = (p_var - p_ctrl) / pooled_se
    p_val = 2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(z_stat)))
    
    return {
        "control_rate": round(p_ctrl, 4),
        "variant_rate": round(p_var, 4),
        "relative_lift_pct": round(((p_var - p_ctrl) / p_ctrl) * 100, 2),
        "z_score": round(z_stat, 3),
        "p_value": round(p_val, 5),
        "statistically_significant": p_val < alpha
    }

# Test output:

items.title: Normal Distribution
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to normal distribution with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

# Production statistical hypothesis test: Normal Distribution
def conduct_ab_significance_test(control_conversions, control_visitors,
                                  variant_conversions, variant_visitors,
                                  alpha=0.05) -> dict:
    # 1. Sample Conversion Proportions
    p_ctrl = control_conversions / control_visitors
    p_var = variant_conversions / variant_visitors
    
    # 2. Pooled Probability
    pooled_p = (control_conversions + variant_conversions) / (control_visitors + variant_visitors)
    pooled_se = np.sqrt(pooled_p * (1 - pooled_p) * (1/control_visitors + 1/variant_visitors))
    
    # 3. Z-Statistic and Two-Sided P-Value
    z_stat = (p_var - p_ctrl) / pooled_se
    p_val = 2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(z_stat)))
    
    return {
        "control_rate": round(p_ctrl, 4),
        "variant_rate": round(p_var, 4),
        "relative_lift_pct": round(((p_var - p_ctrl) / p_ctrl) * 100, 2),
        "z_score": round(z_stat, 3),
        "p_value": round(p_val, 5),
        "statistically_significant": p_val < alpha
    }

# Test output:
# print(conduct_ab_significance_test(120, 1000, 160, 1000))

items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to uniform distribution with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

# Production statistical hypothesis test: Uniform Distribution
def conduct_ab_significance_test(control_conversions, control_visitors,
                                  variant_conversions, variant_visitors,
                                  alpha=0.05) -> dict:
    # 1. Sample Conversion Proportions
    p_ctrl = control_conversions / control_visitors
    p_var = variant_conversions / variant_visitors
    
    # 2. Pooled Probability
    pooled_p = (control_conversions + variant_conversions) / (control_visitors + variant_visitors)
    pooled_se = np.sqrt(pooled_p * (1 - pooled_p) * (1/control_visitors + 1/variant_visitors))
    
    # 3. Z-Statistic and Two-Sided P-Value
    z_stat = (p_var - p_ctrl) / pooled_se
    p_val = 2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(z_stat)))
    
    return {
        "control_rate": round(p_ctrl, 4),
        "variant_rate": round(p_var, 4),
        "relative_lift_pct": round(((p_var - p_ctrl) / p_ctrl) * 100, 2),
        "z_score": round(z_stat, 3),
        "p_value": round(p_val, 5),
        "statistically_significant": p_val < alpha
    }

# Test output:
# print(conduct_ab_significance_test(120, 1000, 160, 1000))

SELECT 
    DATE_TRUNC('month', transaction_date) AS reporting_month,
    product_category,

    ROUND(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 2) AS total_gross_revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(net_profit_usd), 2) AS total_net_profit,

WHERE transaction_date >= '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1 DESC, total_net_profit DESC;

items.title: Standard Errors and Sampling Distributions
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to standard errors and sampling distributions with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

# Production statistical hypothesis test: Standard Errors and Sampling Distributions
def conduct_ab_significance_test(control_conversions, control_visitors,
                                  variant_conversions, variant_visitors,
                                  alpha=0.05) -> dict:
    # 1. Sample Conversion Proportions
    p_ctrl = control_conversions / control_visitors
    p_var = variant_conversions / variant_visitors
    
    # 2. Pooled Probability
    pooled_p = (control_conversions + variant_conversions) / (control_visitors + variant_visitors)
    pooled_se = np.sqrt(pooled_p * (1 - pooled_p) * (1/control_visitors + 1/variant_visitors))
    
    # 3. Z-Statistic and Two-Sided P-Value
    z_stat = (p_var - p_ctrl) / pooled_se
    p_val = 2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(z_stat)))
    
    return {
        "control_rate": round(p_ctrl, 4),
        "variant_rate": round(p_var, 4),
        "relative_lift_pct": round(((p_var - p_ctrl) / p_ctrl) * 100, 2),
        "z_score": round(z_stat, 3),
        "p_value": round(p_val, 5),
        "statistically_significant": p_val < alpha
    }

# Test output:
# print(conduct_ab_significance_test(120, 1000, 160, 1000))

items.title: Statistical Power and Sample Size
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to statistical power and sample size with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

# Production statistical hypothesis test: Statistical Power and Sample Size
def conduct_ab_significance_test(control_conversions, control_visitors,
                                  variant_conversions, variant_visitors,
                                  alpha=0.05) -> dict:
    # 1. Sample Conversion Proportions
    p_ctrl = control_conversions / control_visitors
    p_var = variant_conversions / variant_visitors
    
    # 2. Pooled Probability
    pooled_p = (control_conversions + variant_conversions) / (control_visitors + variant_visitors)
    pooled_se = np.sqrt(pooled_p * (1 - pooled_p) * (1/control_visitors + 1/variant_visitors))
    
    # 3. Z-Statistic and Two-Sided P-Value
    z_stat = (p_var - p_ctrl) / pooled_se
    p_val = 2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(z_stat)))
    
    return {
        "control_rate": round(p_ctrl, 4),
        "variant_rate": round(p_var, 4),
        "relative_lift_pct": round(((p_var - p_ctrl) / p_ctrl) * 100, 2),
        "z_score": round(z_stat, 3),
        "p_value": round(p_val, 5),
        "statistically_significant": p_val < alpha
    }

# Test output:
# print(conduct_ab_significance_test(120, 1000, 160, 1000))

items.title: Simple Linear Regression
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to simple linear regression with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

# Production statistical hypothesis test: Simple Linear Regression
def conduct_ab_significance_test(control_conversions, control_visitors,
                                  variant_conversions, variant_visitors,
                                  alpha=0.05) -> dict:
    # 1. Sample Conversion Proportions
    p_ctrl = control_conversions / control_visitors
    p_var = variant_conversions / variant_visitors
    
    # 2. Pooled Probability
    pooled_p = (control_conversions + variant_conversions) / (control_visitors + variant_visitors)
    pooled_se = np.sqrt(pooled_p * (1 - pooled_p) * (1/control_visitors + 1/variant_visitors))
    
    # 3. Z-Statistic and Two-Sided P-Value
    z_stat = (p_var - p_ctrl) / pooled_se
    p_val = 2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(z_stat)))
    
    return {
        "control_rate": round(p_ctrl, 4),
        "variant_rate": round(p_var, 4),
        "relative_lift_pct": round(((p_var - p_ctrl) / p_ctrl) * 100, 2),
        "z_score": round(z_stat, 3),
        "p_value": round(p_val, 5),
        "statistically_significant": p_val < alpha
    }

# Test output:
# print(conduct_ab_significance_test(120, 1000, 160, 1000))

                                  variant_conversions, variant_visitors,
                                  alpha=0.05) -> dict:

    p_var = variant_conversions / variant_visitors
    
    # 2. Pooled Probability
    pooled_p = (control_conversions + variant_conversions) / (control_visitors + variant_visitors)
    pooled_se = np.sqrt(pooled_p * (1 - pooled_p) * (1/control_visitors + 1/variant_visitors))

title: Data Visualization and Storytelling
description: Transform raw numerical findings into compelling visual narratives using perception principles, chart psychology, storytelling structures, and executive reports.

items.title: Why Data Visualization Matters
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to why data visualization matters with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
-- Production analytical metric specification: Why Data Visualization Matters
SELECT 
    DATE_TRUNC('month', transaction_date) AS reporting_month,
    product_category,
    COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS active_purchasers,
    SUM(quantity) AS units_sold,
    ROUND(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 2) AS total_gross_revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(net_profit_usd), 2) AS total_net_profit,
    ROUND(SUM(net_profit_usd) / NULLIF(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 0) * 100, 2) AS profit_margin_pct
FROM enterprise_analytics.fact_transactions
WHERE transaction_date >= '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1 DESC, total_net_profit DESC;

sections.title: 1. Learning Objectives & Foundational Concepts: Why Data Visualization Matters
sections.explanation: In modern commercial organizations, why data visualization matters is a cornerstone of evidence-based decision making. Rather than relying on intuition or fragmented anecdotal opinions, data analysts harness structured data workflows to uncover empirical realities. By mastering why data visualization matters, analysts learn to transform messy, disparate source data into precise, auditable insights that drive profitability, operational efficiency, and sustainable customer value.
bullets: Core Objective: Master the theoretical and practical mechanics of why data visualization matters.
Beginner-to-Advanced Path: Progress from fundamental definitions to enterprise SQL/Python implementations.
Auditable Integrity: Establish strict data hygiene rules to prevent distorted or misleading conclusions.
Executive Communication: Translate raw statistical parameters into clear strategic business recommendations.

sections.title: 2. Technical Parameter Glossary & Comparison Framework
sections.explanation: When working with why data visualization matters in professional data environments, analysts must master the formal definitions, parameters, and trade-offs. The reference framework below summarizes the primary technical concepts:

rows: Core Dimension (Why Data Visualization Matters)
Foundational variable governing why data visualization matters calculations.
Segmenting enterprise transaction volume across dimensional reporting hierarchies.
Statistical Reliability / Precision
Confidence interval (95%), margin of error, and sample size power.
Validates that observed metrics reflect real business gains rather than random chance.
Aggregation Grain & Integrity
Atomic entity level (e.g. line-item, order header, daily cohort, customer UUID).
Guarantees that joins and aggregations avoid accidental cartesian duplication.
Business KPI & Executive Impact
Target benchmark ratio directly tied to revenue, gross margin, or churn reduction.
Delivers clear visibility to leadership for strategic capital and resource allocation.

sections.explanation: The diagram below outlines the structural pipeline, transformation stages, and analytical dependencies involved when executing why data visualization matters across enterprise data platforms:

sections.title: 5. Practical Case Study, Common Mistakes & Best Practices
sections.explanation: To apply why data visualization matters successfully in commercial production, analysts must recognize common data traps and follow industry-standard analytical protocols:
bullets: Common Mistake: Conflating statistical correlation with direct causation when interpreting metrics.
Common Mistake: Forgetting to filter out cancelled orders or test accounts, inflating revenue calculations.
Best Practice: Always profile distributions, inspect skewness, and isolate outliers before reporting mean averages.
Best Practice: Use parameterized queries and CTEs to document complex SQL transformations for team peer review.
Best Practice: Verify data grain before table joins to prevent fan-out errors that double-count financial numbers.

items.title: Visual Perception and Chart Selection
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to visual perception and chart selection with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
-- Production SQL implementation: Visual Perception and Chart Selection
WITH ranked_transactions AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        order_date,
        order_amount,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date DESC) AS recency_rank,
        SUM(order_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) AS total_customer_lifetime_spend,
        AVG(order_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) AS avg_order_value
    FROM core_ecommerce.fact_orders
    WHERE order_status = 'COMPLETED'
      AND order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '365 days'
)
SELECT 
    customer_id,
    ROUND(total_customer_lifetime_spend, 2) AS ltv_usd,
    ROUND(avg_order_value, 2) AS aov_usd,
    order_date AS most_recent_purchase_date
FROM ranked_transactions
WHERE recency_rank = 1
ORDER BY total_customer_lifetime_spend DESC
LIMIT 100;

items.title: Comparing Values and Distributions
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to comparing values and distributions with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

# Production statistical hypothesis test: Comparing Values and Distributions
def conduct_ab_significance_test(control_conversions, control_visitors,
                                  variant_conversions, variant_visitors,
                                  alpha=0.05) -> dict:
    # 1. Sample Conversion Proportions
    p_ctrl = control_conversions / control_visitors
    p_var = variant_conversions / variant_visitors
    
    # 2. Pooled Probability
    pooled_p = (control_conversions + variant_conversions) / (control_visitors + variant_visitors)
    pooled_se = np.sqrt(pooled_p * (1 - pooled_p) * (1/control_visitors + 1/variant_visitors))
    
    # 3. Z-Statistic and Two-Sided P-Value
    z_stat = (p_var - p_ctrl) / pooled_se
    p_val = 2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(z_stat)))
    
    return {
        "control_rate": round(p_ctrl, 4),
        "variant_rate": round(p_var, 4),
        "relative_lift_pct": round(((p_var - p_ctrl) / p_ctrl) * 100, 2),
        "z_score": round(z_stat, 3),
        "p_value": round(p_val, 5),
        "statistically_significant": p_val < alpha
    }

# Test output:
# print(conduct_ab_significance_test(120, 1000, 160, 1000))

items.title: Visual Perception and Chart Selection
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to visual perception and chart selection with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
-- Production SQL implementation: Visual Perception and Chart Selection
WITH ranked_transactions AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        order_date,
        order_amount,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date DESC) AS recency_rank,
        SUM(order_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) AS total_customer_lifetime_spend,
        AVG(order_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) AS avg_order_value
    FROM core_ecommerce.fact_orders
    WHERE order_status = 'COMPLETED'
      AND order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '365 days'
)
SELECT 
    customer_id,
    ROUND(total_customer_lifetime_spend, 2) AS ltv_usd,
    ROUND(avg_order_value, 2) AS aov_usd,
    order_date AS most_recent_purchase_date
FROM ranked_transactions
WHERE recency_rank = 1
ORDER BY total_customer_lifetime_spend DESC
LIMIT 100;

items.title: Comparing Values and Distributions
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to comparing values and distributions with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

# Production statistical hypothesis test: Comparing Values and Distributions
def conduct_ab_significance_test(control_conversions, control_visitors,
                                  variant_conversions, variant_visitors,
                                  alpha=0.05) -> dict:
    # 1. Sample Conversion Proportions
    p_ctrl = control_conversions / control_visitors
    p_var = variant_conversions / variant_visitors
    
    # 2. Pooled Probability
    pooled_p = (control_conversions + variant_conversions) / (control_visitors + variant_visitors)
    pooled_se = np.sqrt(pooled_p * (1 - pooled_p) * (1/control_visitors + 1/variant_visitors))
    
    # 3. Z-Statistic and Two-Sided P-Value
    z_stat = (p_var - p_ctrl) / pooled_se
    p_val = 2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(z_stat)))
    
    return {
        "control_rate": round(p_ctrl, 4),
        "variant_rate": round(p_var, 4),
        "relative_lift_pct": round(((p_var - p_ctrl) / p_ctrl) * 100, 2),
        "z_score": round(z_stat, 3),
        "p_value": round(p_val, 5),
        "statistically_significant": p_val < alpha
    }

# Test output:
# print(conduct_ab_significance_test(120, 1000, 160, 1000))

title: Business Intelligence and Power BI
description: Build production business intelligence systems in Power BI using Power Query ETL, Star Schema data modeling, advanced DAX calculations, and executive dashboards.

items.title: What Is Business Intelligence?
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to what is business intelligence? with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
-- Production analytical metric specification: What Is Business Intelligence?
SELECT 
    DATE_TRUNC('month', transaction_date) AS reporting_month,
    product_category,
    COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS active_purchasers,
    SUM(quantity) AS units_sold,
    ROUND(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 2) AS total_gross_revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(net_profit_usd), 2) AS total_net_profit,
    ROUND(SUM(net_profit_usd) / NULLIF(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 0) * 100, 2) AS profit_margin_pct
FROM enterprise_analytics.fact_transactions
WHERE transaction_date >= '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1 DESC, total_net_profit DESC;

sections.title: 1. Learning Objectives & Foundational Concepts: What Is Business Intelligence?
sections.explanation: In modern commercial organizations, what is business intelligence? is a cornerstone of evidence-based decision making. Rather than relying on intuition or fragmented anecdotal opinions, data analysts harness structured data workflows to uncover empirical realities. items.title: Introduction to Power BI
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to introduction to power bi with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
// Production DAX Measure: Introduction to Power BI
Revenue YoY Growth % = 
VAR CurrentPeriodRevenue = 
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_Sales[NetRevenue]),
        Dim_Date[IsCurrentFiscalYear] = TRUE()
    )
VAR PriorPeriodRevenue = 
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_Sales[NetRevenue]),
        SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR(Dim_Date[FullDate])
    )
RETURN
    DIVIDE(
        CurrentPeriodRevenue - PriorPeriodRevenue,
        PriorPeriodRevenue,
        0
    )

items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to importing data from excel, csv and databases with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
-- Production SQL implementation: Importing Data from Excel, CSV and Databases
WITH ranked_transactions AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        order_date,
        order_amount,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date DESC) AS recency_rank,
        SUM(order_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) AS total_customer_lifetime_spend,
        AVG(order_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) AS avg_order_value

    WHERE order_status = 'COMPLETED'
      AND order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '365 days'
)
SELECT 
    customer_id,
    ROUND(total_customer_lifetime_spend, 2) AS ltv_usd,
    ROUND(avg_order_value, 2) AS aov_usd,
    order_date AS most_recent_purchase_date
FROM ranked_transactions
WHERE recency_rank = 1
ORDER BY total_customer_lifetime_spend DESC
LIMIT 100;

items.title: Data Types and Data Transformation
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to data types and data transformation with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
-- Production analytical metric specification: Data Types and Data Transformation
SELECT 
    DATE_TRUNC('month', transaction_date) AS reporting_month,
    product_category,
    COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS active_purchasers,
    SUM(quantity) AS units_sold,
    ROUND(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 2) AS total_gross_revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(net_profit_usd), 2) AS total_net_profit,
    ROUND(SUM(net_profit_usd) / NULLIF(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 0) * 100, 2) AS profit_margin_pct
FROM enterprise_analytics.fact_transactions
WHERE transaction_date >= '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1 DESC, total_net_profit DESC;

sections.title: 4. Formulas, Syntax & Hands-On Production Implementation
sections.explanation: The verified production syntax below demonstrates how to compute and evaluate year-over-year and month-over-month analysis using enterprise analytics tools with strict precision and defensive error handling:

codeSnippet.code:
-- Production analytical metric specification: Year-over-Year and Month-over-Month Analysis
SELECT 
    DATE_TRUNC('month', transaction_date) AS reporting_month,
    product_category,
    COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS active_purchasers,
    SUM(quantity) AS units_sold,
    ROUND(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 2) AS total_gross_revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(net_profit_usd), 2) AS total_net_profit,
    ROUND(SUM(net_profit_usd) / NULLIF(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 0) * 100, 2) AS profit_margin_pct
FROM enterprise_analytics.fact_transactions
WHERE transaction_date >= '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1 DESC, total_net_profit DESC;

sections.title: 5. Practical Case Study, Common Mistakes & Best Practices
sections.explanation: To apply year-over-year and month-over-month analysis successfully in commercial production, analysts must recognize common data traps and follow industry-standard analytical protocols:
bullets: Common Mistake: Conflating statistical correlation with direct causation when interpreting metrics.
Common Mistake: Forgetting to filter out cancelled orders or test accounts, inflating revenue calculations.
Best Practice: Always profile distributions, inspect skewness, and isolate outliers before reporting mean averages.
Best Practice: Use parameterized queries and CTEs to document complex SQL transformations for team peer review.
Best Practice: Verify data grain before table joins to prevent fan-out errors that double-count financial numbers.

items.title: Building Power BI Visualizations
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to building power bi visualizations with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
// Production DAX Measure: Building Power BI Visualizations
Revenue YoY Growth % = 
VAR CurrentPeriodRevenue = 
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_Sales[NetRevenue]),
        Dim_Date[IsCurrentFiscalYear] = TRUE()
    )
VAR PriorPeriodRevenue = 
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_Sales[NetRevenue]),
        SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR(Dim_Date[FullDate])
    )
RETURN
    DIVIDE(
        CurrentPeriodRevenue - PriorPeriodRevenue,
        PriorPeriodRevenue,
        0
    )

items.title: What Is Business Intelligence?
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to what is business intelligence? with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
-- Production analytical metric specification: What Is Business Intelligence?
SELECT 
    DATE_TRUNC('month', transaction_date) AS reporting_month,
    product_category,
    COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS active_purchasers,
    SUM(quantity) AS units_sold,
    ROUND(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 2) AS total_gross_revenue,

WHERE transaction_date >= '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1 DESC, total_net_profit DESC;

items.title: Introduction to Power BI
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to introduction to power bi with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
// Production DAX Measure: Introduction to Power BI
Revenue YoY Growth % = 
VAR CurrentPeriodRevenue = 
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_Sales[NetRevenue]),
        Dim_Date[IsCurrentFiscalYear] = TRUE()
    )
VAR PriorPeriodRevenue = 
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_Sales[NetRevenue]),
        SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR(Dim_Date[FullDate])
    )
RETURN
    DIVIDE(
        CurrentPeriodRevenue - PriorPeriodRevenue,
        PriorPeriodRevenue,
        0
    )

items.title: Importing Data from Excel, CSV and Databases
items.contentHeading: Importing Data from Excel, CSV and Databases
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to importing data from excel, csv and databases with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
-- Production SQL implementation: Importing Data from Excel, CSV and Databases
WITH ranked_transactions AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        order_date,
        order_amount,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date DESC) AS recency_rank,
        SUM(order_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) AS total_customer_lifetime_spend,
        AVG(order_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) AS avg_order_value
    FROM core_ecommerce.fact_orders
    WHERE order_status = 'COMPLETED'
      AND order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '365 days'
)
SELECT 
    customer_id,
    ROUND(total_customer_lifetime_spend, 2) AS ltv_usd,
    ROUND(avg_order_value, 2) AS aov_usd,
    order_date AS most_recent_purchase_date
FROM ranked_transactions
WHERE recency_rank = 1
ORDER BY total_customer_lifetime_spend DESC
LIMIT 100;

-- Production analytical metric specification: Data Types and Data Transformation
SELECT 
    DATE_TRUNC('month', transaction_date) AS reporting_month,
    product_category,
    COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS active_purchasers,
    SUM(quantity) AS units_sold,
    ROUND(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 2) AS total_gross_revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(net_profit_usd), 2) AS total_net_profit,

ORDER BY 1 DESC, total_net_profit DESC;

items.title: Introduction to DAX
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to introduction to dax with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
// Production DAX Measure: Introduction to DAX
Revenue YoY Growth % = 
VAR CurrentPeriodRevenue = 
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_Sales[NetRevenue]),
        Dim_Date[IsCurrentFiscalYear] = TRUE()
    )
VAR PriorPeriodRevenue = 
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_Sales[NetRevenue]),
        SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR(Dim_Date[FullDate])
    )
RETURN
    DIVIDE(
        CurrentPeriodRevenue - PriorPeriodRevenue,
        PriorPeriodRevenue,
        0
    )

codeSnippet.code:
// Production DAX Measure: CALCULATE and Filter Context
Revenue YoY Growth % = 
VAR CurrentPeriodRevenue = 
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_Sales[NetRevenue]),
        Dim_Date[IsCurrentFiscalYear] = TRUE()
    )

    CALCULATE(

    )

items.title: Building Power BI Visualizations
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to building power bi visualizations with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
// Production DAX Measure: Building Power BI Visualizations
Revenue YoY Growth % = 
VAR CurrentPeriodRevenue = 
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_Sales[NetRevenue]),
        Dim_Date[IsCurrentFiscalYear] = TRUE()
    )
VAR PriorPeriodRevenue = 
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_Sales[NetRevenue]),
        SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR(Dim_Date[FullDate])
    )
RETURN
    DIVIDE(
        CurrentPeriodRevenue - PriorPeriodRevenue,
        PriorPeriodRevenue,
        0
    )

-- Production analytical metric specification: Refresh Schedules and Gateways
SELECT 
    DATE_TRUNC('month', transaction_date) AS reporting_month,
    product_category,
    COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS active_purchasers,
    SUM(quantity) AS units_sold,
    ROUND(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 2) AS total_gross_revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(net_profit_usd), 2) AS total_net_profit,

items.title: Building a Complete Power BI Business Dashboard
items.contentHeading: Building a Complete Power BI Business Dashboard
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to building a complete power bi business dashboard with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
// Production DAX Measure: Building a Complete Power BI Business Dashboard
Revenue YoY Growth % = 
VAR CurrentPeriodRevenue = 
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_Sales[NetRevenue]),
        Dim_Date[IsCurrentFiscalYear] = TRUE()
    )
VAR PriorPeriodRevenue = 
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_Sales[NetRevenue]),
        SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR(Dim_Date[FullDate])
    )
RETURN
    DIVIDE(
        CurrentPeriodRevenue - PriorPeriodRevenue,
        PriorPeriodRevenue,
        0
    )

questions.prompt: Which foundational analytical practice is essential for producing reliable insights in Business Intelligence and Power BI?

options.label: Relying on unverified gut feelings rather than empirical datasets
Validating data grain, auditing completeness, and using reproducible transformation logic
Deleting test data without creating backup snapshots
Presenting raw unfiltered server logs directly to C-suite executives

questions.explanation: Reliable data analytics requires reproducible data pipelines and strict grain validation to ensure that metrics remain consistent, auditable, and scientifically valid.

questions.prompt: When evaluating business performance trends in Business Intelligence and Power BI, why is inspecting the median often preferable to the mean?

options.label: Because the median is legally mandated by securities regulations
Because the median is resistant to extreme outliers and skewed distributions
Because the median can only be calculated in spreadsheet software
Because the mean always equals zero in commercial datasets

questions.explanation: In skewed distributions (such as customer order values or employee salaries), extreme positive outliers heavily inflate the arithmetic mean, whereas the median reflects the true central typical experience.

questions.explanation: Executive stakeholders require actionable clarity: high-signal visual charts paired with concise narrative insights and clear operational recommendations enable rapid decision-making.

Cartesian fan-out caused by one-to-many relationships without appropriate pre-aggregation
Adding descriptive column aliases with the AS keyword
Sorting the query output with ORDER BY

questions.explanation: Joining a fact table to a child table with multiple matching rows creates a cartesian fan-out, causing SUM aggregations to multiply and report falsely inflated financial figures.

sections.title: 1. Learning Objectives & Foundational Concepts: Introduction to Tableau
sections.explanation: In modern commercial organizations, introduction to tableau is a cornerstone of evidence-based decision making. Rather than relying on intuition or fragmented anecdotal opinions, data analysts harness structured data workflows to uncover empirical realities. By mastering introduction to tableau, analysts learn to transform messy, disparate source data into precise, auditable insights that drive profitability, operational efficiency, and sustainable customer value.
bullets: Core Objective: Master the theoretical and practical mechanics of introduction to tableau.
Beginner-to-Advanced Path: Progress from fundamental definitions to enterprise SQL/Python implementations.
Auditable Integrity: Establish strict data hygiene rules to prevent distorted or misleading conclusions.
Executive Communication: Translate raw statistical parameters into clear strategic business recommendations.

sections.title: 2. Technical Parameter Glossary & Comparison Framework
sections.explanation: When working with introduction to tableau in professional data environments, analysts must master the formal definitions, parameters, and trade-offs. The reference framework below summarizes the primary technical concepts:

rows: Core Dimension (Introduction to Tableau)
Foundational variable governing introduction to tableau calculations.
Segmenting enterprise transaction volume across dimensional reporting hierarchies.
Statistical Reliability / Precision
Confidence interval (95%), margin of error, and sample size power.
Validates that observed metrics reflect real business gains rather than random chance.
Aggregation Grain & Integrity
Atomic entity level (e.g. line-item, order header, daily cohort, customer UUID).
Guarantees that joins and aggregations avoid accidental cartesian duplication.
Business KPI & Executive Impact
Target benchmark ratio directly tied to revenue, gross margin, or churn reduction.
Delivers clear visibility to leadership for strategic capital and resource allocation.

sections.title: 5. Practical Case Study, Common Mistakes & Best Practices
sections.explanation: To apply introduction to tableau successfully in commercial production, analysts must recognize common data traps and follow industry-standard analytical protocols:
bullets: Common Mistake: Conflating statistical correlation with direct causation when interpreting metrics.
Common Mistake: Forgetting to filter out cancelled orders or test accounts, inflating revenue calculations.
Best Practice: Always profile distributions, inspect skewness, and isolate outliers before reporting mean averages.
Best Practice: Use parameterized queries and CTEs to document complex SQL transformations for team peer review.
Best Practice: Verify data grain before table joins to prevent fan-out errors that double-count financial numbers.

questions.prompt: When conducting an enterprise analysis involving 'Introduction to Tableau', what analytical safeguard is essential to prevent false conclusions?

options.label: Deleting all records that do not support the stakeholder's initial hypothesis
Verifying data grain, isolating outliers, and inspecting distributions before computing summary averages
Always using pie charts with 3D effects to maximize visual engagement
Relying strictly on unverified sample sizes of fewer than 5 records

questions.explanation: Defensible analytics requires statistical rigor: validating the table grain prevents double-counting, while inspecting distributions ensures extreme outliers do not skew arithmetic means and lead to flawed business investments.

questions.prompt: How does mastering 'Introduction to Tableau' deliver measurable business value to an executive leadership team?

options.label: By producing lengthy academic papers that take months to decipher
By transforming raw fragmented data into actionable, trustworthy metrics that drive revenue and margin efficiency
By requiring all company employees to manually compute calculations by hand on paper
By preventing business teams from querying the central database

questions.explanation: The ultimate objective of data analytics is commercial impact: eliminating guesswork, empowering leadership with validated insights, and enabling high-conviction decisions that improve business unit economics.

questions.prompt: Which diagnostic metric or indicator is most useful when evaluating the efficiency of Introduction to Tableau?

options.label: How frequently the system crashes without triggering error handlers
The total number of arbitrary comments inside raw configuration files
Error rates, cycle latency, and throughput stability during high-demand execution
Relying solely on subjective developer impressions without data logging

questions.explanation: Evaluating Introduction to Tableau relies on measurable metrics: error frequency, latency percentiles, and throughput consistency under load.

questions.prompt: How does an agile team maintain long-term quality and prevent regression defects in Introduction to Tableau?

options.label: Deploying unreviewed changes directly to production environments
Implementing automated regression test suites, peer reviews, and versioned changelogs
Deleting past test suites to reduce repository storage size
Assuming initial code will remain functional indefinitely without maintenance

questions.explanation: Maintaining high quality in Introduction to Tableau requires automated test coverage, rigorous code review, and version-controlled release management.

questions.prompt: What security consideration must always be enforced when configuring Introduction to Tableau?

options.label: Storing credentials in public version control repositories for easy access
Disabling encryption in transit to maximize network throughput
Granting administrative privileges to all anonymous incoming network requests
Enforcing least privilege access control, secure secret management, and strict input validation

questions.explanation: Security in Introduction to Tableau necessitates least-privilege permissions, encrypted data transit, and strict validation of external inputs.

items.title: Dimensions and Measures
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to dimensions and measures with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
// Production DAX Measure: Dimensions and Measures
Revenue YoY Growth % = 
VAR CurrentPeriodRevenue = 
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_Sales[NetRevenue]),
        Dim_Date[IsCurrentFiscalYear] = TRUE()
    )
VAR PriorPeriodRevenue = 
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_Sales[NetRevenue]),
        SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR(Dim_Date[FullDate])
    )
RETURN
    DIVIDE(
        CurrentPeriodRevenue - PriorPeriodRevenue,
        PriorPeriodRevenue,
        0
    )

items.title: Aggregations and Level of Detail
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to aggregations and level of detail with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
-- Production analytical metric specification: Aggregations and Level of Detail
SELECT 
    DATE_TRUNC('month', transaction_date) AS reporting_month,
    product_category,
    COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS active_purchasers,
    SUM(quantity) AS units_sold,
    ROUND(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 2) AS total_gross_revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(net_profit_usd), 2) AS total_net_profit,
    ROUND(SUM(net_profit_usd) / NULLIF(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 0) * 100, 2) AS profit_margin_pct
FROM enterprise_analytics.fact_transactions
WHERE transaction_date >= '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1 DESC, total_net_profit DESC;

sections.title: 1. Learning Objectives & Foundational Concepts: Introduction to Tableau
sections.explanation: In modern commercial organizations, introduction to tableau is a cornerstone of evidence-based decision making. Rather than relying on intuition or fragmented anecdotal opinions, data analysts harness structured data workflows to uncover empirical realities. sections.title: 5. Practical Case Study, Common Mistakes & Best Practices
sections.explanation: To apply introduction to tableau successfully in commercial production, analysts must recognize common data traps and follow industry-standard analytical protocols:
bullets: Common Mistake: Conflating statistical correlation with direct causation when interpreting metrics.
Common Mistake: Forgetting to filter out cancelled orders or test accounts, inflating revenue calculations.
Best Practice: Always profile distributions, inspect skewness, and isolate outliers before reporting mean averages.
Best Practice: Use parameterized queries and CTEs to document complex SQL transformations for team peer review.
Best Practice: Verify data grain before table joins to prevent fan-out errors that double-count financial numbers.

items.title: Connecting to Data Sources
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to connecting to data sources with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
-- Production analytical metric specification: Connecting to Data Sources
SELECT 
    DATE_TRUNC('month', transaction_date) AS reporting_month,
    product_category,
    COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS active_purchasers,
    SUM(quantity) AS units_sold,
    ROUND(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 2) AS total_gross_revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(net_profit_usd), 2) AS total_net_profit,
    ROUND(SUM(net_profit_usd) / NULLIF(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 0) * 100, 2) AS profit_margin_pct
FROM enterprise_analytics.fact_transactions
WHERE transaction_date >= '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1 DESC, total_net_profit DESC;

items.title: Dimensions and Measures
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to dimensions and measures with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
// Production DAX Measure: Dimensions and Measures
Revenue YoY Growth % = 
VAR CurrentPeriodRevenue = 
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_Sales[NetRevenue]),
        Dim_Date[IsCurrentFiscalYear] = TRUE()
    )
VAR PriorPeriodRevenue = 
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_Sales[NetRevenue]),
        SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR(Dim_Date[FullDate])
    )
RETURN
    DIVIDE(
        CurrentPeriodRevenue - PriorPeriodRevenue,
        PriorPeriodRevenue,
        0
    )

items.title: Calculated Fields
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to calculated fields with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
// Production DAX Measure: Calculated Fields
Revenue YoY Growth % = 
VAR CurrentPeriodRevenue = 
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_Sales[NetRevenue]),
        Dim_Date[IsCurrentFiscalYear] = TRUE()
    )
VAR PriorPeriodRevenue = 
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Fact_Sales[NetRevenue]),
        SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR(Dim_Date[FullDate])
    )
RETURN
    DIVIDE(
        CurrentPeriodRevenue - PriorPeriodRevenue,
        PriorPeriodRevenue,
        0
    )

sections.explanation: The verified production syntax below demonstrates how to compute and evaluate table calculations using enterprise analytics tools with strict precision and defensive error handling:

codeSnippet.code:
-- Production analytical metric specification: Table Calculations
SELECT 
    DATE_TRUNC('month', transaction_date) AS reporting_month,
    product_category,
    COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS active_purchasers,
    SUM(quantity) AS units_sold,
    ROUND(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 2) AS total_gross_revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(net_profit_usd), 2) AS total_net_profit,
    ROUND(SUM(net_profit_usd) / NULLIF(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 0) * 100, 2) AS profit_margin_pct
FROM enterprise_analytics.fact_transactions
WHERE transaction_date >= '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1 DESC, total_net_profit DESC;

items.title: What Is Data Engineering?
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to what is data engineering? with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
-- Production analytical metric specification: What Is Data Engineering?
SELECT 
    DATE_TRUNC('month', transaction_date) AS reporting_month,
    product_category,
    COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS active_purchasers,
    SUM(quantity) AS units_sold,
    ROUND(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 2) AS total_gross_revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(net_profit_usd), 2) AS total_net_profit,
    ROUND(SUM(net_profit_usd) / NULLIF(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 0) * 100, 2) AS profit_margin_pct
FROM enterprise_analytics.fact_transactions
WHERE transaction_date >= '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1 DESC, total_net_profit DESC;

sections.title: 1. Learning Objectives & Foundational Concepts: What Is Data Engineering?
sections.explanation: In modern commercial organizations, what is data engineering? is a cornerstone of evidence-based decision making. Rather than relying on intuition or fragmented anecdotal opinions, data analysts harness structured data workflows to uncover empirical realities. By mastering what is data engineering?, analysts learn to transform messy, disparate source data into precise, auditable insights that drive profitability, operational efficiency, and sustainable customer value.
bullets: Core Objective: Master the theoretical and practical mechanics of what is data engineering?.
Beginner-to-Advanced Path: Progress from fundamental definitions to enterprise SQL/Python implementations.
Auditable Integrity: Establish strict data hygiene rules to prevent distorted or misleading conclusions.
Executive Communication: Translate raw statistical parameters into clear strategic business recommendations.

Guarantees that joins and aggregations avoid accidental cartesian duplication.

Delivers clear visibility to leadership for strategic capital and resource allocation.

sections.title: 5. Practical Case Study, Common Mistakes & Best Practices
sections.explanation: To apply what is data engineering? successfully in commercial production, analysts must recognize common data traps and follow industry-standard analytical protocols:
bullets: Common Mistake: Conflating statistical correlation with direct causation when interpreting metrics.
Common Mistake: Forgetting to filter out cancelled orders or test accounts, inflating revenue calculations.
Best Practice: Always profile distributions, inspect skewness, and isolate outliers before reporting mean averages.
Best Practice: Use parameterized queries and CTEs to document complex SQL transformations for team peer review.
Best Practice: Verify data grain before table joins to prevent fan-out errors that double-count financial numbers.

items.title: Introduction to BigQuery
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to introduction to bigquery with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
-- Production SQL implementation: Introduction to BigQuery
WITH ranked_transactions AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        order_date,
        order_amount,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date DESC) AS recency_rank,
        SUM(order_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) AS total_customer_lifetime_spend,
        AVG(order_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) AS avg_order_value
    FROM core_ecommerce.fact_orders
    WHERE order_status = 'COMPLETED'
      AND order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '365 days'
)
SELECT 
    customer_id,
    ROUND(total_customer_lifetime_spend, 2) AS ltv_usd,
    ROUND(avg_order_value, 2) AS aov_usd,
    order_date AS most_recent_purchase_date
FROM ranked_transactions
WHERE recency_rank = 1
ORDER BY total_customer_lifetime_spend DESC
LIMIT 100;

items.title: Introduction to BigQuery
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to introduction to bigquery with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
-- Production SQL implementation: Introduction to BigQuery
WITH ranked_transactions AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        order_date,
        order_amount,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date DESC) AS recency_rank,
        SUM(order_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) AS total_customer_lifetime_spend,
        AVG(order_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) AS avg_order_value
    FROM core_ecommerce.fact_orders
    WHERE order_status = 'COMPLETED'
      AND order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '365 days'
)
SELECT 
    customer_id,
    ROUND(total_customer_lifetime_spend, 2) AS ltv_usd,
    ROUND(avg_order_value, 2) AS aov_usd,
    order_date AS most_recent_purchase_date
FROM ranked_transactions
WHERE recency_rank = 1
ORDER BY total_customer_lifetime_spend DESC
LIMIT 100;

sections.title: 4. Formulas, Syntax & Hands-On Production Implementation
sections.explanation: The verified production syntax below demonstrates how to compute and evaluate data quality monitoring using enterprise analytics tools with strict precision and defensive error handling:

codeSnippet.code:
-- Production analytical metric specification: Data Quality Monitoring
SELECT 
    DATE_TRUNC('month', transaction_date) AS reporting_month,
    product_category,
    COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS active_purchasers,
    SUM(quantity) AS units_sold,
    ROUND(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 2) AS total_gross_revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(net_profit_usd), 2) AS total_net_profit,
    ROUND(SUM(net_profit_usd) / NULLIF(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 0) * 100, 2) AS profit_margin_pct
FROM enterprise_analytics.fact_transactions
WHERE transaction_date >= '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1 DESC, total_net_profit DESC;

sections.title: 5. Practical Case Study, Common Mistakes & Best Practices

Best Practice: Verify data grain before table joins to prevent fan-out errors that double-count financial numbers.

items.title: What Is Predictive Analytics?
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to what is predictive analytics? with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
-- Production analytical metric specification: What Is Predictive Analytics?
SELECT 
    DATE_TRUNC('month', transaction_date) AS reporting_month,
    product_category,
    COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS active_purchasers,
    SUM(quantity) AS units_sold,
    ROUND(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 2) AS total_gross_revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(net_profit_usd), 2) AS total_net_profit,
    ROUND(SUM(net_profit_usd) / NULLIF(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 0) * 100, 2) AS profit_margin_pct
FROM enterprise_analytics.fact_transactions
WHERE transaction_date >= '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1 DESC, total_net_profit DESC;

sections.title: 1. Learning Objectives & Foundational Concepts: What Is Predictive Analytics?

items.title: Training, Validation and Test Datasets
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to training, validation and test datasets with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

# Production statistical hypothesis test: Training, Validation and Test Datasets
def conduct_ab_significance_test(control_conversions, control_visitors,
                                  variant_conversions, variant_visitors,
                                  alpha=0.05) -> dict:
    # 1. Sample Conversion Proportions
    p_ctrl = control_conversions / control_visitors
    p_var = variant_conversions / variant_visitors
    
    # 2. Pooled Probability
    pooled_p = (control_conversions + variant_conversions) / (control_visitors + variant_visitors)
    pooled_se = np.sqrt(pooled_p * (1 - pooled_p) * (1/control_visitors + 1/variant_visitors))
    
    # 3. Z-Statistic and Two-Sided P-Value
    z_stat = (p_var - p_ctrl) / pooled_se
    p_val = 2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(z_stat)))
    
    return {
        "control_rate": round(p_ctrl, 4),
        "variant_rate": round(p_var, 4),
        "relative_lift_pct": round(((p_var - p_ctrl) / p_ctrl) * 100, 2),
        "z_score": round(z_stat, 3),
        "p_value": round(p_val, 5),
        "statistically_significant": p_val < alpha
    }

# Test output:
# print(conduct_ab_significance_test(120, 1000, 160, 1000))

items.title: Regression vs Classification
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to regression vs classification with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

# Production statistical hypothesis test: Regression vs Classification
def conduct_ab_significance_test(control_conversions, control_visitors,
                                  variant_conversions, variant_visitors,
                                  alpha=0.05) -> dict:
    # 1. Sample Conversion Proportions
    p_ctrl = control_conversions / control_visitors
    p_var = variant_conversions / variant_visitors
    
    # 2. Pooled Probability
    pooled_p = (control_conversions + variant_conversions) / (control_visitors + variant_visitors)
    pooled_se = np.sqrt(pooled_p * (1 - pooled_p) * (1/control_visitors + 1/variant_visitors))
    
    # 3. Z-Statistic and Two-Sided P-Value
    z_stat = (p_var - p_ctrl) / pooled_se
    p_val = 2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(z_stat)))
    
    return {
        "control_rate": round(p_ctrl, 4),
        "variant_rate": round(p_var, 4),
        "relative_lift_pct": round(((p_var - p_ctrl) / p_ctrl) * 100, 2),
        "z_score": round(z_stat, 3),
        "p_value": round(p_val, 5),
        "statistically_significant": p_val < alpha
    }

# Test output:
# print(conduct_ab_significance_test(120, 1000, 160, 1000))

items.title: Cross-Validation and Model Selection
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to cross-validation and model selection with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
-- Production SQL implementation: Cross-Validation and Model Selection
WITH ranked_transactions AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        order_date,
        order_amount,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date DESC) AS recency_rank,
        SUM(order_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) AS total_customer_lifetime_spend,
        AVG(order_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) AS avg_order_value
    FROM core_ecommerce.fact_orders
    WHERE order_status = 'COMPLETED'
      AND order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '365 days'
)
SELECT 
    customer_id,
    ROUND(total_customer_lifetime_spend, 2) AS ltv_usd,
    ROUND(avg_order_value, 2) AS aov_usd,
    order_date AS most_recent_purchase_date
FROM ranked_transactions
WHERE recency_rank = 1
ORDER BY total_customer_lifetime_spend DESC
LIMIT 100;

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Production analytics pipeline: Introduction to Scikit-learn
def analyze_business_performance(csv_path: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    # 1. Load dataset with strict parsing
    df = pd.read_csv(csv_path, parse_dates=['order_date'])
    
    # 2. Data hygiene: handle missing values and remove duplicates
    df = df.drop_duplicates(subset=['order_id'])
    df['discount_pct'] = df['discount_pct'].fillna(0.0)
    
    # 3. Feature engineering: Net Revenue calculation
    df['net_revenue'] = df['gross_amount'] * (1 - df['discount_pct'])
    
    # 4. Multidimensional aggregation
    summary = df.groupby(['region', 'customer_segment']).agg(
        total_orders=('order_id', 'count'),
        total_revenue=('net_revenue', 'sum'),
        avg_order_value=('net_revenue', 'mean'),
        std_deviation=('net_revenue', 'std')
    ).reset_index()
    
    summary['revenue_pct'] = (summary['total_revenue'] / summary['total_revenue'].sum()) * 100
    return summary.sort_values(by='total_revenue', ascending=False)

items.title: Linear Regression
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to linear regression with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

# Production statistical hypothesis test: Linear Regression
def conduct_ab_significance_test(control_conversions, control_visitors,
                                  variant_conversions, variant_visitors,
                                  alpha=0.05) -> dict:
    # 1. Sample Conversion Proportions
    p_ctrl = control_conversions / control_visitors
    p_var = variant_conversions / variant_visitors
    
    # 2. Pooled Probability
    pooled_p = (control_conversions + variant_conversions) / (control_visitors + variant_visitors)
    pooled_se = np.sqrt(pooled_p * (1 - pooled_p) * (1/control_visitors + 1/variant_visitors))
    
    # 3. Z-Statistic and Two-Sided P-Value
    z_stat = (p_var - p_ctrl) / pooled_se
    p_val = 2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(z_stat)))
    
    return {
        "control_rate": round(p_ctrl, 4),
        "variant_rate": round(p_var, 4),
        "relative_lift_pct": round(((p_var - p_ctrl) / p_ctrl) * 100, 2),
        "z_score": round(z_stat, 3),
        "p_value": round(p_val, 5),
        "statistically_significant": p_val < alpha
    }

# Test output:
# print(conduct_ab_significance_test(120, 1000, 160, 1000))

items.title: Regression Metrics
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to regression metrics with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

# Production statistical hypothesis test: Regression Metrics
def conduct_ab_significance_test(control_conversions, control_visitors,
                                  variant_conversions, variant_visitors,
                                  alpha=0.05) -> dict:
    # 1. Sample Conversion Proportions
    p_ctrl = control_conversions / control_visitors
    p_var = variant_conversions / variant_visitors
    
    # 2. Pooled Probability
    pooled_p = (control_conversions + variant_conversions) / (control_visitors + variant_visitors)
    pooled_se = np.sqrt(pooled_p * (1 - pooled_p) * (1/control_visitors + 1/variant_visitors))
    
    # 3. Z-Statistic and Two-Sided P-Value
    z_stat = (p_var - p_ctrl) / pooled_se
    p_val = 2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(z_stat)))
    
    return {
        "control_rate": round(p_ctrl, 4),
        "variant_rate": round(p_var, 4),
        "relative_lift_pct": round(((p_var - p_ctrl) / p_ctrl) * 100, 2),
        "z_score": round(z_stat, 3),
        "p_value": round(p_val, 5),
        "statistically_significant": p_val < alpha
    }

# Test output:
# print(conduct_ab_significance_test(120, 1000, 160, 1000))

items.title: Experimentation and A/B Testing
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to experimentation and a/b testing with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

# Production statistical hypothesis test: Experimentation and A/B Testing
def conduct_ab_significance_test(control_conversions, control_visitors,
                                  variant_conversions, variant_visitors,
                                  alpha=0.05) -> dict:
    # 1. Sample Conversion Proportions
    p_ctrl = control_conversions / control_visitors
    p_var = variant_conversions / variant_visitors
    
    # 2. Pooled Probability
    pooled_p = (control_conversions + variant_conversions) / (control_visitors + variant_visitors)
    pooled_se = np.sqrt(pooled_p * (1 - pooled_p) * (1/control_visitors + 1/variant_visitors))
    
    # 3. Z-Statistic and Two-Sided P-Value
    z_stat = (p_var - p_ctrl) / pooled_se
    p_val = 2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(z_stat)))
    
    return {
        "control_rate": round(p_ctrl, 4),
        "variant_rate": round(p_var, 4),
        "relative_lift_pct": round(((p_var - p_ctrl) / p_ctrl) * 100, 2),
        "z_score": round(z_stat, 3),
        "p_value": round(p_val, 5),
        "statistically_significant": p_val < alpha
    }

# Test output:
# print(conduct_ab_significance_test(120, 1000, 160, 1000))

sections.title: 4. Formulas, Syntax & Hands-On Production Implementation
sections.explanation: The verified production syntax below demonstrates how to compute and evaluate communicating predictive results and limitations using enterprise analytics tools with strict precision and defensive error handling:

codeSnippet.code:
-- Production analytical metric specification: Communicating Predictive Results and Limitations
SELECT 
    DATE_TRUNC('month', transaction_date) AS reporting_month,
    product_category,
    COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS active_purchasers,
    SUM(quantity) AS units_sold,
    ROUND(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 2) AS total_gross_revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(net_profit_usd), 2) AS total_net_profit,
    ROUND(SUM(net_profit_usd) / NULLIF(SUM(gross_revenue_usd), 0) * 100, 2) AS profit_margin_pct
FROM enterprise_analytics.fact_transactions
WHERE transaction_date >= '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1 DESC, total_net_profit DESC;

sections.title: 5. Practical Case Study, Common Mistakes & Best Practices

bullets: Common Mistake: Conflating statistical correlation with direct causation when interpreting metrics.

Best Practice: Use parameterized queries and CTEs to document complex SQL transformations for team peer review.
Best Practice: Verify data grain before table joins to prevent fan-out errors that double-count financial numbers.

items.title: Training, Validation and Test Datasets
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to training, validation and test datasets with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

# Production statistical hypothesis test: Training, Validation and Test Datasets
def conduct_ab_significance_test(control_conversions, control_visitors,
                                  variant_conversions, variant_visitors,
                                  alpha=0.05) -> dict:
    # 1. Sample Conversion Proportions
    p_ctrl = control_conversions / control_visitors
    p_var = variant_conversions / variant_visitors
    
    # 2. Pooled Probability
    pooled_p = (control_conversions + variant_conversions) / (control_visitors + variant_visitors)
    pooled_se = np.sqrt(pooled_p * (1 - pooled_p) * (1/control_visitors + 1/variant_visitors))
    
    # 3. Z-Statistic and Two-Sided P-Value
    z_stat = (p_var - p_ctrl) / pooled_se
    p_val = 2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(z_stat)))
    
    return {
        "control_rate": round(p_ctrl, 4),
        "variant_rate": round(p_var, 4),
        "relative_lift_pct": round(((p_var - p_ctrl) / p_ctrl) * 100, 2),
        "z_score": round(z_stat, 3),
        "p_value": round(p_val, 5),
        "statistically_significant": p_val < alpha
    }

# Test output:
# print(conduct_ab_significance_test(120, 1000, 160, 1000))

items.title: Regression vs Classification
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to regression vs classification with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

# Production statistical hypothesis test: Regression vs Classification
def conduct_ab_significance_test(control_conversions, control_visitors,
                                  variant_conversions, variant_visitors,
                                  alpha=0.05) -> dict:
    # 1. Sample Conversion Proportions
    p_ctrl = control_conversions / control_visitors
    p_var = variant_conversions / variant_visitors
    
    # 2. Pooled Probability
    pooled_p = (control_conversions + variant_conversions) / (control_visitors + variant_visitors)
    pooled_se = np.sqrt(pooled_p * (1 - pooled_p) * (1/control_visitors + 1/variant_visitors))
    
    # 3. Z-Statistic and Two-Sided P-Value
    z_stat = (p_var - p_ctrl) / pooled_se
    p_val = 2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(z_stat)))
    
    return {
        "control_rate": round(p_ctrl, 4),
        "variant_rate": round(p_var, 4),
        "relative_lift_pct": round(((p_var - p_ctrl) / p_ctrl) * 100, 2),
        "z_score": round(z_stat, 3),
        "p_value": round(p_val, 5),
        "statistically_significant": p_val < alpha
    }

# Test output:
# print(conduct_ab_significance_test(120, 1000, 160, 1000))

items.title: Cross-Validation and Model Selection
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to cross-validation and model selection with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
-- Production SQL implementation: Cross-Validation and Model Selection
WITH ranked_transactions AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        order_date,
        order_amount,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date DESC) AS recency_rank,
        SUM(order_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) AS total_customer_lifetime_spend,
        AVG(order_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) AS avg_order_value
    FROM core_ecommerce.fact_orders
    WHERE order_status = 'COMPLETED'
      AND order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '365 days'
)
SELECT 
    customer_id,
    ROUND(total_customer_lifetime_spend, 2) AS ltv_usd,
    ROUND(avg_order_value, 2) AS aov_usd,
    order_date AS most_recent_purchase_date
FROM ranked_transactions
WHERE recency_rank = 1
ORDER BY total_customer_lifetime_spend DESC
LIMIT 100;

items.title: Introduction to Scikit-learn
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to introduction to scikit-learn with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Production analytics pipeline: Introduction to Scikit-learn
def analyze_business_performance(csv_path: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    # 1. Load dataset with strict parsing
    df = pd.read_csv(csv_path, parse_dates=['order_date'])
    
    # 2. Data hygiene: handle missing values and remove duplicates
    df = df.drop_duplicates(subset=['order_id'])
    df['discount_pct'] = df['discount_pct'].fillna(0.0)
    
    # 3. Feature engineering: Net Revenue calculation
    df['net_revenue'] = df['gross_amount'] * (1 - df['discount_pct'])
    
    # 4. Multidimensional aggregation
    summary = df.groupby(['region', 'customer_segment']).agg(
        total_orders=('order_id', 'count'),
        total_revenue=('net_revenue', 'sum'),
        avg_order_value=('net_revenue', 'mean'),
        std_deviation=('net_revenue', 'std')
    ).reset_index()
    
    summary['revenue_pct'] = (summary['total_revenue'] / summary['total_revenue'].sum()) * 100
    return summary.sort_values(by='total_revenue', ascending=False)

# Execution sample
# summary_df = analyze_business_performance("sales_data_2026.csv")

items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to linear regression with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

# Production statistical hypothesis test: Linear Regression
def conduct_ab_significance_test(control_conversions, control_visitors,
                                  variant_conversions, variant_visitors,
                                  alpha=0.05) -> dict:
    # 1. Sample Conversion Proportions
    p_ctrl = control_conversions / control_visitors
    p_var = variant_conversions / variant_visitors
    
    # 2. Pooled Probability
    pooled_p = (control_conversions + variant_conversions) / (control_visitors + variant_visitors)
    pooled_se = np.sqrt(pooled_p * (1 - pooled_p) * (1/control_visitors + 1/variant_visitors))
    
    # 3. Z-Statistic and Two-Sided P-Value
    z_stat = (p_var - p_ctrl) / pooled_se
    p_val = 2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(z_stat)))
    
    return {
        "control_rate": round(p_ctrl, 4),
        "variant_rate": round(p_var, 4),
        "relative_lift_pct": round(((p_var - p_ctrl) / p_ctrl) * 100, 2),
        "z_score": round(z_stat, 3),
        "p_value": round(p_val, 5),
        "statistically_significant": p_val < alpha
    }

# Test output:
# print(conduct_ab_significance_test(120, 1000, 160, 1000))

items.title: Regression Metrics
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to regression metrics with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

# Production statistical hypothesis test: Regression Metrics
def conduct_ab_significance_test(control_conversions, control_visitors,
                                  variant_conversions, variant_visitors,
                                  alpha=0.05) -> dict:
    # 1. Sample Conversion Proportions
    p_ctrl = control_conversions / control_visitors
    p_var = variant_conversions / variant_visitors
    
    # 2. Pooled Probability
    pooled_p = (control_conversions + variant_conversions) / (control_visitors + variant_visitors)
    pooled_se = np.sqrt(pooled_p * (1 - pooled_p) * (1/control_visitors + 1/variant_visitors))
    
    # 3. Z-Statistic and Two-Sided P-Value
    z_stat = (p_var - p_ctrl) / pooled_se
    p_val = 2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(z_stat)))
    
    return {
        "control_rate": round(p_ctrl, 4),
        "variant_rate": round(p_var, 4),
        "relative_lift_pct": round(((p_var - p_ctrl) / p_ctrl) * 100, 2),
        "z_score": round(z_stat, 3),
        "p_value": round(p_val, 5),
        "statistically_significant": p_val < alpha
    }

# Test output:
# print(conduct_ab_significance_test(120, 1000, 160, 1000))

items.title: Experimentation and A/B Testing
items.contentDescription: Comprehensive guide to experimentation and a/b testing with architectural data flowcharts, formula/code syntax, and real-world commercial analytics examples.

codeSnippet.code:
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

# Production statistical hypothesis test: Experimentation and A/B Testing
def conduct_ab_significance_test(control_conversions, control_visitors,
                                  variant_conversions, variant_visitors,
                                  alpha=0.05) -> dict:
    # 1. Sample Conversion Proportions
    p_ctrl = control_conversions / control_visitors
    p_var = variant_conversions / variant_visitors
    
    # 2. Pooled Probability
    pooled_p = (control_conversions + variant_conversions) / (control_visitors + variant_visitors)
    pooled_se = np.sqrt(pooled_p * (1 - pooled_p) * (1/control_visitors + 1/variant_visitors))
    
    # 3. Z-Statistic and Two-Sided P-Value
    z_stat = (p_var - p_ctrl) / pooled_se
    p_val = 2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(z_stat)))
    
    return {
        "control_rate": round(p_ctrl, 4),
        "variant_rate": round(p_var, 4),
        "relative_lift_pct": round(((p_var - p_ctrl) / p_ctrl) * 100, 2),
        "z_score": round(z_stat, 3),
        "p_value": round(p_val, 5),
        "statistically_significant": p_val < alpha
    }

# Test output:
# print(conduct_ab_significance_test(120, 1000, 160, 1000))
